verses.1: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go and speak to Pharaoh, saying, ‘I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his servants, so that they may not listen to my words.’”
verses.2: And so that you may tell your sons and grandsons about what I did to the Egyptians, and about the plagues I sent upon them. Then they will know that I am Jehovah.
verses.3: And Moses and Aaron went before Pharaoh. They said to him, “As the LORD, the God of the Israelites, has commanded, ‘Until when will you continue to refuse to obey me? Then I will send a plague upon your people, and they will worship me.’”
verses.4: For if you do not send me my people away, then I will bring back a hundred thousand men from your land tomorrow.
verses.5: And he covered the eyes of the earth, so that he couldn’t see the land at all. He ate up all the leaves that remained for you from the fields, and he devoured all the trees that grew in the forests.
verses.6: And they filled your houses, and the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all the nations of the Egyptians. They did not see your ancestors or their ancestors since they first appeared on the earth until today. They left and went away from Pharaoh’s presence.
verses.7: And the servants of Pharaoh said to him, “As long as this continues, it will be a hardship for us to send these people and make them serve Jehovah our God. After all, we will know that Egypt has been destroyed.”
verses.8: And he brought Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh. He said to them, “Go and worship Yahweh, your God. Who is going to go first?”
verses.9: And Moses said, “In our youth and in our old age, we will go forth in our own land and in our own gardens. We will go forth on the day of God’s celebration for us.”
verses.10: And He said to them, “May it be so, O LORD! As I send you out, and your flocks with you. But see, evil is coming against you.”
verses.11: Do not do so, O kings! Serve Jehovah instead. For this is what you ask of Him. He drove them away from Pharaoh’s presence.
verses.12: And the LORD said to Moses, “Put your hand over the land of Egypt. May it be cursed, and may it become a land of suffering for the Egyptians. It will be a place where every plant on the ground will be destroyed, just as the barley was destroyed.”
verses.13: And Moses laid his hand on the land of Egypt. Then God sent a wind across the land, day and night. The wind carried away all the locusts from the land.
verses.14: And the locusts rose up over all the land of Egypt. They spread their wings over every border of Egypt, in great numbers. No locusts had ever been like this before; and no more will there be such locusts after them.
verses.15: And it covered the entire earth with its shadow. The earth became dark. It ate up all the plants on the earth, as well as all the fruits of the trees that were left standing. No grass or plants remained in any of the fields or gardens throughout Egypt.
verses.16: And Pharaoh hurriedly called for Moses and Aaron. He said, “I have sinned against you, God, and against you too.”
verses.17: And now, I have sinned. But this time, please pray to the LORD your God, and let Him remove this death from me.
verses.18: And he went out from Pharaoh’s presence and pleaded with Yahweh.
verses.19: And Jehovah made the wind very strong. He raised up the waves, and they were fixed in place. No wave remained in all the borders of Egypt.
verses.20: And Jehovah strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not send away the children of Israel.
verses.21: And the LORD said to Moses, “Put your hand over the heavens, so that there will be darkness over the land of Egypt. There will be night for seven days.”
verses.22: And Moses raised his hand over the heavens, and darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.
verses.23: No one saw their brothers, and no one got up from under them for three days. For all the children of Israel, there was light in their places of rest.
verses.24: And Pharaoh called out to Moses and said, “Go and worship Yahweh. But bring along your offerings with you; they will also be given to you as a gift.”
verses.25: And Moses said, “You also give us offerings and sacrifices. We will make them for the LORD our God.”
verses.26: And even our possessions will go with us. They won’t remain behind. For from us, these things are taken away in order that we may serve the LORD our God. And we won’t know what we will be serving the LORD until we reach our destination.
verses.27: And Jehovah strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, so that he did not send them away.
verses.28: And Pharaoh said to him, “Go away from me! Keep your distance from me, so that you won’t see my face. For on the day you see my face, you will die.”
verses.29: And Moses said, “So you have spoken. I will not see your face again.”
